title: Mass of the split majority distribution
statement: Let $m\ge 0$, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $h$ be a pair consisting of two signs and $t$ a tuple of $2m+1$ signs. Under the distribution obtained by independently sampling the two coordinates of $h$ and the coordinates of $t$ from the sign law that assigns probability $p$ to $+1$ and $1-p$ to $-1$, the probability mass of $(h,t)$ is the product of the probability mass of $h$ and the probability mass of $t$ under their respective product distributions.
